newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 6.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Greece is facing the danger of the European Commission cutting off Cohesion Fund financing if it does not manage to get the deficit down to convergence programme targets by next year. A meeting in Brussels today is expected to issue an official warning to Athens.

--The government yesterday failed to take the final decisions on the difficult 1997 budget. The discussion will continue today. The problem is reaching a workable compromise between achieving convergence programme targets and keeping a lid on social and political reactions.
--Scams cost the state 2.2 trillion drachmas. Deputy Finance Minister George Drys says that the state will only recoup 100 billion drachmas over the next two years.
--The sinking of the gunboat off Samos on Monday night was a chain of tragic mistakes. The merchant marine and navy lock horns over who is to blame.
--Both captains of the gunboat and passenger ship Samaina are to blame for Monday night's collision.
--Clinton wins another four years in the White House and Athens prepares to get him to stick to his campaign promises on a US package to resolve issues such as the Cyprus problem and the Aegean.

--Intense consultations under way between leading members of the main opposition New Democracy party to find a solution to the thorny leadership issue, despite president Miltiades Evert's insistence yesterday that he will not step down.
